title: I Took the Darts-League Board Signup to the Captain Who Hogged Three

parts.text: I signed board C at 7:04 p.m. and captain Moss had already hung three names including a ghost. The chalk said: ONE BOARD. ONE TEAM. NO GHOST HOURS. I was twenty-eight, pub player, holding a chalk slip. Moss shrugged. "Captains are the oche." I photographed the chalk, the slip, and the three names. Then I asked for the board log. At 7:11 the bar manager pinged why Moss's name was on two extra boards. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The bar manager can see Moss's three names on board C during my signup.

social.video_title: The captain hogged three boards with a ghost team — Part 1/2
social.description: Darts league, chalk signup, a ghost hour. I logged the extra boards. Would you have asked the bar?

parts.text: Moss called it seeding until the manager asked for the still. I printed the log, the chalk, and the slip. Two names erased. Moss ran one board and told the next captain seeding was always about optics. Optics is a word captains use when chalk exists. Signup now has a second line: CAPTAINS ARE NOT THE OCHE. I keep board C. Moss brown-bags his jokes. The pub finally looks like a slip, not a takeover. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.video_title: Captains are not the oche — Part 2/2
social.description: Board log, erased ghosts, and a second line. Was seeding ever three boards?
